translation:
Wh-what's with you guys? I thought your
business with us was over?

As soon as we entered the room, the
president was already trying to shut us out.

Well, not that I can blame him—Haruhi is known
to cause trouble.
Come now, don't we share a neighborly bond?

Koizumi swiftly pushed back against the door
and entered the room with his easy smile.

Even a seasoned salesman wouldn't be able to
make such a magnificent entrance.

Th-thus begins our misfortune. You guys
cause nothing but trouble!

I'd like to make it very clear that Haruhi is the
only one causing trouble.

We just want to ask for more details about
the fabled class 1-10 or whatever it's called.

We need proof that it's nonsense so we can
get Haruhi to quit chasing this ghost story…

…because horrors on a greater scale than
the seven wonders of our school lie in wait.

World destruction or alteration—that kind of
thing might actually be possible…
W-we've already told your leader everything.

We think you may have left out a few
things—unintentionally, of course.

People don't just hand out their recollections
to those they feel uncomfortable with.

Data is required. Preferably as detailed as
possible.
E-even if you say that…

Koizumi approaching with his easy smile, and
Nagato stoically demanding information—

Between these two, the president was served
a different flavor of intimidation than Haruhi's.

This atmosphere… It's as if they're leading him
to confess to some non-existent murder.

If you guys put too much pressure on him, he
won't be able to remember anything.
Well, there's certainly truth in that.

Let's each take turns to make sure we get
everything he knows out of him.
So—we'll start with…
Let's have Nagato kick us off.
Understood. Who is the witness?

…Fine then. Let's just make sure this is the
last time, okay?
No promises, but we'll do the best we can.

You—answer their questions quickly so we
can get them out of here.

The president called out to one of the club
members.

We're in the middle of a very delicate and
sensitive operation.

We can't keep getting interrupted like this—
actually, we're already behind schedule…

Now that he's not the target of the
questioning, he seems much more carefree.
I won't forget about his complaining though.
Hearsay? Direct experience?
Ah… I actually experienced it myself.
Alone? Group?
Umm, I was alone…

List all evidence that led to the conclusion of
class 10's existence.
Huh…? L-list it?

I assume there are criteria by which you
recognized it as class 1-10.
Y-yes—the plate said 1-10.
Be specific.
S-specific?

Not visual information—attribute changes or
the effects of other physical phenomena.
H-huuh?!

For example, were there fluctuations in mass?
Did the time oscillation hold a normal value?

As you'd expect, I have no idea what's with
these questions.

For the time being, could you at least try and
tell us about it in more detail?
R-right…
U-umm, there was this feeling, and…
…What else?
Other than that, well, umm…
Nagato's line of questioning continued.

Occasionally she went quiet and motionlessly
stared—it seemed to put pressure on him.

He revealed that they decided to hold a
summer camp to create an original game.

He told us this completely unprompted,
sending the president into a panic.
Oooh… Please just give me a break already!

I just mistook what I saw, okay? Please, no
more!
He ended up crying and denying everything.

If Miss Suzumiya heard this and simply
accepted it, the problem would be solved.

Except it's Haruhi, so that's never going to
work.

Though it would have been better if Haruhi
were here to witness it for herself.

Not that I'd expect her to just stand there
and quietly watch.

Koizumi—you're good at cross-examining,
aren't you?

Cross-examination? That's a remarkable way
of putting it, though I won't deny your claim.
How dare you say that so shamelessly!
You want me to start questioning?
Go for it.

Well then, how about we begin by discussing
the objective of this summer camp?

That's got nothing to do with the mystery,
does it?

Aren't you being hasty in deciding whether it's
related or not?

Disregarding whether or not you actually
witnessed such a curiosity…

…I'd like to pin down the basic information, if
you wouldn't mind.

I don't have cause to tell outsiders like you—
it's a computer society secret, you know?

Oh my, so you have something you wish to
hide, do you?

Shall I take that to mean it would trouble you
if we found out?
Th-that's not the case whatsoever!

So you want me to take your word for it
without knowing the details… Ah, that's tricky.

He's just spitting out these sinister lines with
a smile on his face.

I feel a little sorry for the club president—my
bad for choosing Koizumi.

…We're developing an original game for the
school festival.

I can't tell you any more about the game until
it's finished and released.

I understand. As follows, your group has been
spending a long time staring at monitors.

That would certainly make your eyes
tired—perhaps even impair your vision.

Incidentally, the witness was someone other
than yourself, so who is that person?
…It's me.

Then would you mind running us through the
whole event? Please recount all the details.
Koizumi's questioning continued on and on.

By the time it was over, the whole computer
society had been robbed of their vigor.

Even the ones who weren't questioned looked
as if all the life had been siphoned out of them.
It was a truly pitiful scene.
Even I'm somehow tired…

It seems we've heard everything worth
hearing.

That's because you bullied him down to his
core. He won't be back on his feet for a while.
Naturally, I can't help but feel sorry for them.
Let's just head back to Haruhi for now.

But before that, maybe I should have a quick
word with the other two…?

So you didn't find anything significant…
right?
Nagato—aren't you tired?
I'm fine.
I guess that was a stupid question.

Although, this alien-made organic android
does eat and sleep.

Actually, I've never confirmed that she
sleeps, but—

What I'm trying to say is that everything I've
seen her do so far seems human-like…
…could that all just be in my head?

She might also just be acting tough after I
showed concern for her.
Don't overdo it, Nagato.

Through thick and thin, in the end, you're
always my last hope.
…Understood.
Koizumi, aren't you beat?

Oh my, isn't that rare—having you direct
your concern towards me.

The fact that you're being needlessly sar-
castic tells me you've got plenty of energy.
Truly a pity.

I apologize for failing to live up to your
expectations.
Snide 'til the bitter end, this guy.

I guess such a merciless brigade chief would
have equally merciless subordinates…

He said something I couldn't ignore, but see-
ing his condition, it was hard to argue back.

Our reputation is getting worse and worse,
and it seems too late to do anything about it.
We thank you for your cooperation.

Don't let anyone know that we're making an
original game.
Especially Miss Brigade Chief.
That's not an issue, of course. Fret not.
That smile is so easy it's suspicious.

For some reason, I'm starting to feel bad for
those computer society members.
Why?

I feel as if we exhibited decorum in our
questioning…
These two…

Didn't you see how utterly spent they were?
That was a bit excessive, right?
We can't afford to go easy on them.

Abnormal space is currently forming in the
school, and it's likely worsening by the second.
Until we stop Haruhi.

They planted the seed, so I personally don't
have sympathy to spare.

…I suppose so. We have to quickly persuade
Haruhi to leave the school grounds.
By the way, I chanced upon this earlier.

Koizumi took out a memory card and showed
me.

Might I ask "where” you happened to chance
upon it?

Outside of the computer society room.
I think they must have dropped it.

It's pretty shady to say you "chanced upon
it” if its just something they dropped.

I believe it contains the data for the original
game they're producing.
I wonder if we could use it?
For what?

To draw Miss Suzumiya's attention away from
the seven wonders, of course.

Ah, so that's why this bastard's smile looked
so suspicious.

Man, you'll really do anything if it's for
Haruhi's sake, huh, Koizumi?

If it's for the sake of defending the world, I
don't much care what others think of me.
Give it back.

I'll return it if you so insist, but are you really
sure about this?

We can't play a game that's still mid-
development. Haruhi would quickly get bored.
Either way—it's important to them, isn't it?
Well, I suppose you're right.

Not to mention, it might be more beneficial to
use it to earn a favor from them.

We have four mysteries. We might not be able
to convince Haruhi with the first—class 1-10.
If you say so…
Alright, then it's settled.

Well then, I guess I'd better go back and
return this thing.

Defending the world, huh? I hate that it's
true.
Dissatisfied?

Yeah I'm dissatisfied—not that there's
anything I can do about it.

I take issue with the fact that the safety of
the world depends on Haruhi's mood.

Even Koizumi—you can call it his job, but he's
earnestly trying to protect the world.

They got us into this mess, so I'll have them
be the ones to pay for it.

They won't be able to make games anyways if
the world ceases to exist.

Telling myself that, I decided to ignore the
feelings of guilt for now.
Choose Nagato
Choose Koizumi
Talk to Nagato
Talk to Koizumi
Give it back.
Defending the world, huh?
